sources: CCE 1SW Wk1 Day 5 canonical lesson, Xello Matchmaker and Career-Match Reflection, accessed 2026-08-15.
Xello licensed educator guide, Matchmaker Assessment, current local district copy.
Private teacher-created AVID source deck, inherited layout and lesson choreography only.
recovery: Use the teacher demo, licensed guide, sentence frames, and private Canvas response. A paper sort can support reflection but does not count as Matchmaker completion; record the access status for supervised catch-up.

slides.lookFor: Students enter with Chromebooks closed until the privacy and prerequisite directions are stated.
slides.pivot: Keep this cover up while the teacher demo account and Completion Standards report are ready.

slides.lookFor: Students are seated and ready for an individual assessment block.
slides.pivot: Move students to lower-distraction seats before launching Xello.

texts:
Today’s Lesson
Model the scale
Answer 39 questions
Open Find out why
Reflect privately

Chromebook
ClassLink + Xello
Private Canvas reflection
No screenshots of results

Discussion

One activity you like
One task you avoid
What might those answers suggest about work?
slides.lookFor: Students can name the assessment, Find out why, and private reflection as three separate actions.
slides.pivot: Do not show a real student profile; keep the demo account ready.

slides.lookFor: One liked activity, one avoided task, and a tentative connection—not a permanent label.
slides.pivot: Allow fictional or course-only examples; no hobby or family disclosure is required.

images.alt: Licensed Xello Matchmaker educator guide showing the current assessment overview

texts:
Your answers change the order of career matches.
A surprising or weak match is still useful evidence.
You can change, learn, and investigate before deciding anything.
slides.lookFor: Students understand that the result is a starting point, not a grade or destiny.
slides.pivot: Ask for a silent thumbs-sideways if a student has ever changed an interest.

texts: Matchmaker opens only after the earlier After high school goal is complete. STATUS: ready • prerequisite missing • login/access issue • absent. The teacher records the status; students do not submit screenshots.
slides.lookFor: Every student is quickly assigned the ready or catch-up route without public disclosure.
slides.pivot: Students with a missing prerequisite use supervised catch-up; do not consume the whole class launch.

texts:
LIKE VERY MUCH
LIKE
NOT SURE
DISLIKE
DISLIKE VERY MUCH

Answer honestly. Do not choose the same response repeatedly just to finish.
slides.lookFor: Students can distinguish strong like, uncertainty, and strong dislike.
slides.pivot: Read the scale aloud and model one neutral example through the demo account.

texts: Choose one sample career result • Open Find out why • Notice which interests raised or lowered the match. Model with the teacher demo—not a real student profile.
slides.lookFor: Students can explain that a match score is connected to specific interest answers.
slides.pivot: Use the visible text model if video or demo access fails.

slides.lookFor: Every ready student opens Matchmaker, not another About Me quiz.
slides.pivot: Project the tested campus route; record access issues rather than sharing credentials.

texts: Read each statement • Use the full scale • Ask for a read-aloud when a word is unclear. Quiet individual work: the goal is an honest pattern, not the fastest finish.
slides.lookFor: First lap: all ready students are in Matchmaker and reading rather than rapid-clicking.
slides.pivot: If one third stalls on vocabulary, pause for one sample read-aloud and restart the quiet block.
slides.trim: Do not trim the 28-minute assessment runway; trim optional video or whole-group discussion.

texts:
WORK BLOCK 2
Finish the first 39 questions.
Review the career matches that appear.
Open one career.
Do not move to another About Me assessment.
Second lap: varied responses, steady reading, and the correct assessment.
slides.lookFor: Second lap: students use varied responses; finished students are reviewing matches, not starting another quiz.
slides.pivot: If a student will not finish by minute 40, record catch-up and allow a teacher-sample reflection start.

texts: Use Find out why Before You Reflect

Find out why
Which interest raised or lowered this match?
What part fits or surprises you?

A result can be useful even when you dislike it.
slides.lookFor: Final lap: each finished student opens one career and Find out why.
slides.pivot: Use the teacher-sample result for students whose assessment is still pending.

texts:
1. What result surprised you, and why?
2. What did Find out why show about one match?
3. Give one example of how an interest affected a career match.
Text or private oral conference. Score the reasoning—not whether the student likes the result.
slides.lookFor: All three prompts have a reason or example; students do not post screenshots or public results.
slides.pivot: Use the three sentence frames, speech-to-text, or private conference record.

texts:
COMPLETE
PREREQUISITE MISSING
LOGIN / ACCESS ISSUE
ABSENT
Completion Standards is the platform record. Schedule supervised catch-up for the last three.
slides.lookFor: Teacher status list matches the Completion Standards report and private reflection records.
slides.pivot: Do not call out statuses aloud; record them quietly while students close.

texts:
A result that surprised me was ____. One interest that changed a match was ____. One question I still have is ____.

slides.lookFor: Students submit one private response or have a named catch-up status.
slides.pivot: Use a silent close; protect privacy and finish the status record.
